text.p: Outgoing Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday that his government had considered issuing five-year Treasury bills to make it more difficult for populist political parties to bring about budget deficits.

"In the previous cabinet meeting together with the finance minister (Robert Zile) we yet again supported the issuing of five-year T-bills by signing the relevant document," Shkele told a news conference.
"This was our last attempt to create an obstacle so that those who want to gallop towards inflation would stumble," Shkele said.
He said talks about the impossibility of a balanced 1997 budget caused concerns about political parties possibly willing to raise salaries and pensions on borrowed finds in a pre-election year.
Shkele said that this would throw Latvia back into a spiral of inflation.

"The Latvian state budget is in its best-ever shape," Shkele said. Its fiscal deficit was currently at 0.9 percent of GDP compared to late 1995, when his goverment took office and it was 4.5 percent of GDP.
The state budget by July 31 showed a 36.7 million lat surplus, compared to a 1996 deficit of 22 million lats, he added.
"It would be a pity if this is sacrificed in the name of political slogans," he added.
